description:
Writes a whole structure of thoughts, links, notes, tags and aliases in a single call. Call it once you have decomposed some material (an article, a document, a discussion) into several connected thoughts — creating them one by one at that volume is slow and breaks halfway.
Thoughts reference each other by tempId, arbitrary labels you invent yourself; the server substitutes real identifiers. A parent may be either a tempId from this batch or the UUID of an existing thought, which is how a new branch grafts onto what the brain already holds.
Search with brain_search first: some of the thoughts may already exist, and linking to them beats creating duplicates.

brainId.description: Brain identifier. Take it from brain_list — never guess it.

deduplicate.description: Skip creating a thought when its parent already has one of that name under the same relation. On by default, which makes re-running a batch safe. A thought of that name under another relation is neither reused nor made again: it fails, with its identifier. So do two of that name under the same relation.

links.description: Extra links on top of the hierarchy. These are what turn a set of thoughts into a graph — use them freely and label them. Neither a type nor a tag can be the parent end of a child or parent link: set a type with typeId and a tag with tagIds.

thoughts.description: The batch's thoughts. Order does not matter; dependencies resolve themselves.

aliases.description: Alternate names. A thought that already existed keeps its own and gains these. Saving a brain's first alias makes that brain require TheBrain 15.0.621 or later on every device, so write aliases only when the user wants them in this brain.

note.description: Note in Markdown. Written to a new thought, and to one that existed only if it has no note: a note that is there is kept, and the result says so.

parent.description: A tempId from this batch or the UUID of an existing thought. Without it the thought is left unlinked, and a second run of the plan makes it again. Not a type or a tag: those go in typeId and tagIds.

relation.description: How this thought relates to its parent. Usually child. Refused without a parent.

tagIds.description: Tag identifiers from brain_list_types_and_tags, not tempIds.

tempId.description: Label for references within this batch, e.g. "rag" or "t1".

name: brain_ingest
